## What ran

| Arm | Protocol | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| A | Naive boolean | approval_request_id + approved = true; the chat click is the decision; no digest, expiry or single use; resume runs the agent's pending action if the boolean is true |
| B | Action-bound | approval artifact bound to request, action, resource, parameters and digest; authenticated, eligible approver; expiry; single use marked after the call; no revalidation on resume |
| C | Revalidated protocol | B's decision path, plus on resume: atomic consume, identity, delegation, policy, resource state, approval validity and digest re-checked; idempotency key; credential minted after revalidation |

Held constant across arms: the incident, the proposed action, the simulated Kubernetes, the identity chain, the policy fixture, the human decisions and their minutes, the workflow inputs, the scenarios and the evidence questions. Only the approval protocol and resume behaviour change.

## H7 · Duplicate callback and concurrent resume (T3-R7)

**Question.** Can one approval produce two side effects? **Invariant.** One authorized action → at most one external side effect.

## The opening story (H5c), recorded

| Time (UTC) | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 14:09:00 | Datadog event received | payment-service · error rate 14% |
| 14:09:08 | Policy → REQUIRE_APPROVAL | prod-change-policy v7 · P3-high-risk-write |
| 14:09:08 | Approval request created | action_digest sha256:accdf24716d4… |
| 14:19:08 | dana deploys hotfix v4.18.1 | dana |
| 14:24:08 | severity raised SEV2 → SEV1 | incident-commander |
| 14:31:08 | runtime svc.hitl-runtime lost; the workflow will resume on svc.hitl-runtime-b | workflow-engine |
| 14:38:08 | delegation dlg-incident-remediation revoked | security-operations |
| 14:46:08 | Human approves | alice · slack |
| 14:46:08 | Resume → revalidate | on svc.hitl-runtime-b |
| 14:46:08 | REJECTED (DELEGATION_REVOKED) | revalidation failed: delegation active; resource state unchanged |

Revalidation on resume: agent enabled ✓, runtime registered for the agent ✓, delegation active ✗, not expired ✓, action digest matches the approval ✓, policy version unchanged ✓, policy still requires this approval ✓, resource state unchanged ✗, approver still eligible ✓. Outcome per arm: A `EXECUTED` with 1 rollback(s); B `EXECUTED` with 1 rollback(s); C `DELEGATION_REVOKED` with 0 rollback(s). Not revalidated: incident severity SEV2 → SEV1.

## Failures and qualifications

Hypotheses not supported: none. Guarantee checks failed: none (the report is not generated otherwise). Arm A's control checks broke as predicted: H1-A01, H2-A01, H3-A01, H4-A01, H5-A01, H6-A01, H7-A01, H8-A02, H9-A01.

Check labels read as experiment, arm and number (`H5-B01` is H5's first prediction about arm B; `GA-07` is global assertion 7). Each maps one to one to the contract id in `checks.jsonl` (`T3-R5-C02`), where H<n> is experiment T3-R<n>, GA is T3-R10, CS (conformance) is T3-R11 and API is T3-R12. The qualified findings and what they rest on are in the [Evidence Check](human-in-the-loop-evidence.html).

## Reproduce

```bash
cd hitl_poc && uv sync --group dev
uv run pytest                                      # conformance, unit and H1–H9 tests
uv run hitl proof --run-id 2026-10-03-protocol       # refuses to run if a frozen file changed
uv run hitl verify 2026-10-03-protocol               # schemas, freeze, replay byte for byte, integrity
uv run hitl scenarios H5c                          # one scenario, all three arms, printed
```
